Introduction to EarthFlux

Source: vignettes/earthflux-introduction.Rmd
earthflux-introduction.Rmd
library(EarthFlux)

Purpose

Land-Surface Energy and Water Fluxes from Earth Observation Data

EarthFlux aims to provide a reproducible workflow to estimate spatially distributed actual evapotranspiration (ETa) following the conceptual chain

MODIS + METRIC + GWR → ETa

This vignette describes the workflow that EarthFlux implements step by step. Version 0.1.0 is the first, experimental release: the METRIC core physics (net radiation, soil heat flux, anchor pixels, sensible and latent heat flux, instantaneous and daily ET), the meteorological forcing (station tables, quality control, reference ET) and its regionalization (including GWR) are available as functions, and the MODIS preprocessing is internal, with an example scene shipped as the dataset cauquenes_modis. The integrated earthflux() workflow does not exist yet. Most METRIC formulations are candidates pending verification against the primary reference, and no result shown in the package documentation should be interpreted as validated.

Conceptual workflow

  1. Surface state. Satellite products (MODIS first) are converted into sensor-independent physical variables: land surface temperature (K), broadband albedo, NDVI, leaf area index and surface emissivity.
  2. Meteorological forcing. Weather station data are quality controlled and, optionally, regionalised into spatial surfaces, for example with geographically weighted regression (GWR).
  3. Surface energy balance (METRIC). Net radiation (Rn), soil heat flux (G), anchor pixel calibration, aerodynamic resistance (rah), the near-surface temperature difference (dT) and sensible heat flux (H) are computed by separate functions. Latent heat flux is the residual LE = Rn - G - H.
  4. Evapotranspiration. LE is converted to instantaneous ET, to the reference ET fraction (ETrF) and finally to daily ETa using reference evapotranspiration.
  5. Diagnostics. Each step reports quality flags instead of silently modifying anomalous values.

Research question

The use of spatially varying meteorological forcing in METRIC is treated as a hypothesis. EarthFlux is designed so that the same METRIC chain can be run with (i) a single representative weather station, (ii) a reference spatial interpolation method and (iii) GWR, and compared against independent observations.

Net radiation

The surface net radiation is the first available component. All fluxes are instantaneous at the satellite overpass, in W m-2; the input values below are illustrative.

ef_net_radiation(
  rs_in = 800, albedo = 0.20, rl_in = 320,
  rl_out = 450.0846, emissivity = 0.98
)
#> [1] 503.5154

Example scene

The dataset cauquenes_modis holds the MODIS surface state of the Cauquenes province (Maule Region, Chile) for 15 February 2019. The emitted longwave radiation of its cells follows from the land surface temperature (K) and the broadband emissivity:

r <- terra::unwrap(cauquenes_modis)
rl_out <- ef_rl_out(
  lst = terra::values(r[["lst"]], mat = FALSE),
  emissivity = terra::values(r[["emissivity"]], mat = FALSE)
)
summary(rl_out) # W m-2; NA outside the province and where LST is missing
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.     NAs 
#>   383.4   444.1   467.8   458.1   476.2   489.6    5937

Next steps

The integrated earthflux() workflow (milestone M5) will chain these components with automatic inputs (MODIS products, elevation model and gridded weather forcing) and documented presets. The scientific comparison of a single station, simple interpolation and GWR as meteorological forcing (milestone M6) comes after it.
